arxiv-1502-05131.title: Affective Music Information Retrieval
arxiv-1502-05131.creator: Ju-Chiang Wang, Yi-Hsuan Yang, and Hsin-Min WangInstitute of Information Science,Academia Sinica, Taipei, Taiwan
arxiv-1502-05131.description: Abstract Much of the appeal of music lies in its power to convey emotions/moods and to evoke them in listeners. In consequence, the past decade witnessed a growing interest in modeling emotions from musical signals in the music information retrieval (MIR) community.

arxiv-2201-08094.title: Stability of smooth solitary waves in the b b -Camassa–Holm equation
arxiv-2201-08094.creator: Stéphane Lafortune, Dmitry E. Pelinovsky
arxiv-2201-08094.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Stéphane Lafortune, Dmitry E. Pelinovsky. We derive the precise stability criterion for smooth solitary waves in the b b -family of Camassa–Holm equations. The smooth solitary waves exist on the constant background. In the integrable cases b = 2 b=2 and b = 3 b=3 , we show analytically that the stability criterion is satisfied and smooth solitary waves are orbitally stable with respect to perturbations in H 3 ​ ( ℝ ) H^{3}(\mathbb{R}) .

arxiv-2203-06807.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Amir Reza Rahmani, Linwei Li, Brian Vanover, Colin Bertrand, Shourabh Rawat. Community Question Answering (CQA) has gained increasing popularity in many domains. Mortgage is a complex and dynamic industry, and a flexible and efficient CQA platform can potentially enhance the quality of service for mortgage officers significantly.

arxiv-2206-03135.title: Microwave cavity-free hole burning spectroscopy of Er 3+ :Y 2 SiO 5 at millikelvin temperatures
arxiv-2206-03135.creator: A. Mladenov, N. Pankratova, D. Sholokhov, V. Manucharyan, R. Gross, P. A. Bushev, N. Kukharchyk
arxiv-2206-03135.description: Abstract Efficient quantum memory is of paramount importance for long-distance quantum communications, as well as for complex large-scale computing architectures. We investigate the capability of Er 3+ :Y 2 SiO 5 crystal to serve as a quantum memory for the travelling microwave photons by employing techniques developed for dense optical ensembles.

arxiv-2312-11185.title: A classification of Fourier summation formulas and crystalline measures
arxiv-2312-11185.creator: Felipe Gonçalves
arxiv-2312-11185.description: Abstract . We completely classify Fourier summation formulas, and in particular, all crystalline measures with quadratic decay. Our classification employs techniques from almost periodic functions, Hermite-Biehler functions, de Branges spaces and Poisson representation. We show how our classification generalizes recent results of Kurasov & Sarnak and Olevskii & Ulanovskii.

arxiv-2403-12185.title: Halperin States of Particles and Holes in Ideal Time Reversal Invariant Pairs of Chern Bands and The Fractional Quantum Spin Hall Effect in Moiré MoTe 2
arxiv-2403-12185.creator: Inti Sodemann Villadiego
arxiv-2403-12185.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Inti Sodemann Villadiego. An experiment in moiré MoTe 2 bilayers reported the first observation of a topologically ordered state with zero Hall conductivity and half of the edge conductance of a standard time-reversal invariant quantum spin Hall insulator. This state is believed to emerge at total filling one of a pair of bands with Chern numbers C = ± 1 C=\pm 1 related by time reversal symmetry.

arxiv-2407-13029.title: Bayesian Inference and the Principle of Maximum Entropy
arxiv-2407-13029.creator: Duncan K. Foley, Ellis Scharfenaker
arxiv-2407-13029.description: Abstract Bayes’ theorem incorporates distinct types of information through the likelihood and prior. Direct observations of state variables enter the likelihood and modify posterior probabilities through consistent updating. Information in terms of expected values of state variables modify posterior probabilities by constraining prior probabilities to be consistent with the information.

arxiv-2408-01322.title: A Robotics-Inspired Scanpath Model Reveals the Importance of Uncertainty and Semantic Object Cues for Gaze Guidance in Dynamic Scenes
arxiv-2408-01322.creator: Vito Mengers, Nicolas Roth, Oliver Brock, Klaus Obermayer, Martin Rolfs
arxiv-2408-01322.description: Abstract The objects we perceive guide our eye movements when observing real-world dynamic scenes. Yet, gaze shifts and selective attention are critical for perceiving details and refining object boundaries. Object segmentation and gaze behavior are, however, typically treated as two independent processes.

arxiv-2409-06230.title: Contests with sequential moves: An experimental study
arxiv-2409-06230.creator: Arthur B. Nelson, Dmitry Ryvkin
arxiv-2409-06230.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Arthur B. Nelson, Dmitry Ryvkin. We study experimentally contests in which players make investment decisions sequentially, and information on prior investments is revealed between stages. Using a between-subject design, we consider all possible sequences in contests of three players and test two major comparative statics of the subgame-perfect Nash equilibrium: The positive effect of the number of stages on aggregate investment and earlier mover advantage.

arxiv-2409-19205.title: A Search for z = 5 z=5 H α \alpha and H β + \beta+ [O III] Dual-Line Emitting Galaxies in the JWST CEERS Field: Implications for the AGN Abundance Facilities: JWST,HST astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2013 ) , Galfit ( Peng et al. 2010 )

arxiv-2409-19205.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Jingsong Guo, Masafusa Onoue, Kohei Inayoshi, Dale D. Kocevski, Steven L. Finkelstein, Micaela B. Bagley, Elizabeth J. McGrath. The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) has enabled us to uncover faint galaxies and active galactic nuclei (AGNs) in the early universe. Taking advantage of the unique filter combination used in the Cosmic Evolution Early Release Science Survey (CEERS) program, we perform an extensive photometric search of galaxies emitting strong H β + \beta+ [O III] and H α \alpha lines.

arxiv-2410-01879.title: Black Hole Accretion and Spin-up through Stellar Collisions in Dense Star Clusters
arxiv-2410-01879.creator: Fulya Kıroğlu, Kyle Kremer, Sylvia Biscoveanu, Elena González Prieto, Frederic A. Rasio
arxiv-2410-01879.description: Abstract Dynamical interactions in dense star clusters could significantly influence the properties of black holes, leaving imprints on their gravitational-wave signatures. While previous studies have mostly focused on repeated black hole mergers for spin and mass growth, this work examines the impact of physical collisions and close encounters between black holes and (noncompact) stars.

arxiv-2411-06776.title: Machine vision-aware quality metrics for compressed image and video assessment
arxiv-2411-06776.creator: Mikhail Dremin, Konstantin Kozhemyakov, Ivan Molodetskikh, Malakhov Kirill, Sagitov Artur, Dmitriy Vatolin
arxiv-2411-06776.description: Abstract A main goal in developing video-compression algorithms is to enhance human-perceived visual quality while maintaining file size. But modern video-analysis efforts such as detection and recognition, which are integral to video surveillance and autonomous vehicles, involve so much data that they necessitate machine-vision processing with minimal human intervention.

arxiv-2502-01585.title: The φ \varphi Curve: The Shape of Generalization through the Lens of Norm-based Capacity Control
arxiv-2502-01585.creator: Yichen Wang, Yudong Chen, Lorenzo Rosasco, Fanghui Liu
arxiv-2502-01585.description: Abstract Understanding how the test risk scales with model complexity is a central question in machine learning. Classical theory is challenged by the learning curves observed for large over-parametrized deep networks. Capacity measures based on parameter count typically fail to account for these empirical observations.

arxiv-2506-10899.title: Demystifying Spectral Feature Learning for Instrumental Variable Regression
arxiv-2506-10899.creator: Dimitri Meunier, Antoine Moulin, Jakub Wornbard, Vladimir R. Kostic, Arthur Gretton
arxiv-2506-10899.description: Abstract We address the problem of causal effect estimation in the presence of hidden confounders, using nonparametric instrumental variable (IV) regression. A leading strategy employs spectral features - that is, learned features spanning the top eigensubspaces of the operator linking treatments to instruments.

arxiv-2506-18576.title: A Modular Taxonomy for Hate Speech Definitions and Its Impact on Zero-Shot LLM Classification Performance
arxiv-2506-18576.creator: Matteo Melis, Gabriella Lapesa, Dennis Assenmacher
arxiv-2506-18576.description: Abstract Detecting harmful content is a crucial task in the landscape of NLP applications for Social Good, with hate speech being one of its most dangerous forms. But what do we mean by hate speech, how can we define it, and how does prompting different definitions of hate speech affect model performance? The contribution of this work is twofold.
